inputs.original_text: White House border czar Tom Homan on Tuesday did not rule out the presence of immigration enforcement at polling places, asking what Democrats are “afraid of.” Homan’s comments, made during an appearance on “The Charlie Kirk Show,” are the latest in the back and forth as the Trump administration gives inconsistent answers over whether they...
inputs.modified_text: This message treats the possibility of immigration enforcement as proof of intimidation, but that is a political leap, not evidence. Eligible citizens should be able to vote without interference, and officials should give clear answers. That does not mean immigration law should be suspended around polling places or that any uncertainty proves a plan to frighten voters. Respect for democracy requires both protecting lawful voting and upholding the rule of law—not turning every question about enforcement into a partisan accusation.
